english.title: Fail to inspect snare for wild animal every day
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having set in position a snare which was of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to any wild animal coming into contact with it, failed, without reasonable excuse, to inspect it at least once every day that it remained in position
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(3) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) From the 17th October 2023, section 48 of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023 amends section 11 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 so this offence no longer applies in Wales. For the offence applying England from the 17th October 2023, see H101443.
(ii) See section 21(7) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) See section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) This offence will be used for lawfully set snares but can also be used for unlawfully set snares. For illegal snare setting see offence wordings H4658, H4659, H4662, H4663, H4667, H4668, H4669 and H4670.
(v) See also offence wordings H4678 and H4679 failing to cause/permit the daily inspection of snares.
(vi) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(vii) See section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant having set in position a snare which was of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to any wild animal coming into contact with it, failed, without reasonable excuse, to inspect it at least once every day that it remained in position.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (section 21(5)).

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date was unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 20 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
